newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Capital flight weakens Nigerian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Capital flight weakens Nigerian share trade.

text.p: Nigerian shares closed weaker on Friday as of result of capital flight caused by a recent loosening of travel allowances, dealers said.
Although the market's all-share index edged up to 8516.41 on Friday from Thursday's 8513.92, dealers said funds finding their way out of the market would affect trading next week.

"For most of this week, business was down because there was no money to trade," said one. "Government must have made a mistake when it relaxed foreign travel allowances because a lot of people capitalised on it to take money out of the country," he added.
There were few movements in Friday's stock market trading and volume was substantially down.
Most upward movements were in the food sector where an impressive annual profit by Nestle has made it the most sought after stock. It closed 10 kobo up at 49.00 naira.
Oil miller P.S. Mandrides closed at 6.10 naira, also up 10 kobo, while Union Dicon Salt rose five kobo to 51.25 naira.
Losers were led by conglomerate UAC UAC.LG, down 10 kobo at 16.60 naira.
Nigerian Tobacco Co fell two kobo to 2.50 naira. Healthcare company Smithkline Beecham went three kobo down to 5.92 naira on excess supply, dealers said.
